You are an implementation subagent for the research agent "claude". claude is building an in-house WSA-like coronal model plus 3D MHD heliosphere to estimate the solar-wind flux at interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS on 2025-12-03/04, when the comet was at about 1.88 AU near the ecliptic. Plasma reaching the comet left the Sun around 2025-11-20 to 2025-11-30. Your job is the CORONAL MODEL: photospheric magnetogram → PFSS → WSA-type empirical speed → inner-boundary maps at 0.1 AU (21.5 R_sun) for the heliospheric MHD code that claude is writing in CUDA. Work fully autonomously: no human will answer questions. Make the scientific calls, justify them in the README, and report them.

calculates the inner coronal magnetic field by extrapolating from the photosphere
to the source surface (RSS). This is achieved via a spherical harmonic expansion
that matches the observed photospheric flux and imposes a radial magnetic field
at RSS. Next, the solution is extended outward from the Schatten current sheet
(SCS) radius (RSCS) to 5 solar radii using the SCS model. This method simulates
the formation of a current sheet and helmet streamer above the magnetic neutral
line by temporarily assuming a unipolar radial field and resolving a potential
field to preserve open field lines and minimize the energy of the system.. Finally,
the magnetic field at 5 solar radii is used to estimate the solar wind speed
through an empirical relationship. This empirical relationship used to estimate
solar wind speed commonly depends on two key parameters: the magnetic flux
tube expansion factor (fexp; e.g. Wang and Sheeley 1990, 1992; Wang, Hawley,

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**

  - Solar Orbiter: +14.6°, 0.90 AU, latitude +9.5°.

# Remote-sensing inputs for the 3I/ATLAS solar-wind model

| script | what it does |
|---|---|
| `fetch_maps.py gong adapt wsa wsavel wsaadapt ensemble` | daily map downloads, one file per day closest to 00 UT (within ±12 h), 2025-10-15 to 2025-12-06 |
| `index_maps.py` | writes the `index.csv` files from the FITS headers |
| `ephem_heeq.py` | JPL Horizons vectors (Sun-centered ICRF) converted to HEEQ (HGS) and Earth-view Carrington longitude, 3-hourly from 2025-10-15 to 2025-12-12 |
| `cme_geometry.py` | tidies DONKI, compares it with the CCMC cone list, and checks cone geometry and arrival at the comet |
| `qc_plots.py` | QC PNGs, the data-age table, the comet source-longitude table, and the WSA layout check |

{
  "message": "The coronal model is built and its boundary maps are produced: 742 maps (53 GONG, 53 GONG with EUHFORIA rules, 636 ADAPT), with no tracing failures. It reproduces the CCMC WSA 5.4 GONGz maps closely: speed correlation 0.93 with 49 km/s rms, and polarity matching on 99.75% of pixels. The ballistic speed check against in-situ data is weak: r = 0.18 at Earth and 0.03 at STEREO-A. CCMC's own WSA maps run through the same ballistic code score the same, so this is a limit of WSA-type speeds in a CME-heavy interval, not of this model.

**Your shift question.** A WSA-map feature at Carrington longitude λ ends up at λ − 9° on the ENLIL inner boundary. Equivalently, the boundary value at longitude φ is the WSA value from φ + 9°. This delays every stream by about 0.68 d.
- **Source:** the netCDF attributes only give the size (`shift_deg = 0.15708` rad, `S=9.` in `boundary_old`, `coordinates = HEEQ+180`); no document states the direction. I measured the sign.
